pr_title: posix: env: support for environ, getenv(), setenv(), unsetenv()
pr_body:
**Note: Coding Guidelines failures are false positives**

Support getting and setting POSIX environment variables. Additionally, the thread-safe BSD variant `getenv_r()` is provided.

`environ`, `getenv()`, `setenv()`, and `unsetenv()` are required by the `POSIX_SINGLE_PROCESS` Option Group as detailed in Section E.1 of IEEE-1003.1-2017.

The `POSIX_SINGLE_PROCESS` Option Group is required for PSE51, PSE52, PSE53, and PSE54 conformance, and is otherwise mandatory for any POSIX conforming system as per Section A.2.1.3 of IEEE-1003-1.2017.

This lets us do fun things like what is shown below in the Zephyr shell:
```shell
uart:~$ posix env 
  set    get    unset
uart:~$ posix env get 
uart:~$ posix env set FOO=BAR
uart:~$ posix env get
FOO=BAR
uart:~$ posix env get FOO
BAR
uart:~$ posix env unset FOO
uart:~$ posix env set " 42 BCD" "No Problem!"
uart:~$ posix env get
uart:~$ posix env set "_BcD" "No Problem!"
uart:~$ posix env get
_BcD=No Problem!
uart:~$ posix env unset _BcD
```

App and library code can then query values from the environment, as a relatively simple and portable way of steering the behaviour of code at runtime.

Some notes:

* "poorly conditioned" variable names are dropped silently in the shell, which matches bash (or at least zsh)
* the Zephyr shell does not perform shell variable expansion at this time; in other words `echo "$VALUE"` will not work as one might expect

Possible future improvements:
* Heh... half joking, but adding shell variable expansion (or even an actual POSIX shell)
* this implementation is optimized for size (a speed optimization could maybe use hash tables)
* another future optimization for safety would be to have a malloc-free implementation
* a possibly nice feature for the shell would be to enable tab completions of names with `env get <tab>`
* another future improvement would be to use Kconfig / iterable sections to optionally enable some default environment variables to be populated (e.g. `HOME`, `PWD`, ...).
* another future improvement might be to add hooks for "dynamic" environment variables like `$RANDOM`.

Fixes #66861
Fixes #66862

Output of `twister --retry-failed=3 -i -T tests/posix`

> Seems like these functions should live in libc/common

I would say that statement is maximally 25% true; `getenv()` is part of ISO C but `environ`, `setenv()`, and `unsetenv()` are not. It would not be possible for an external ISO C library to use those POSIX features with Zephyr if they were located in `libc/common`.

I do agree that ISO C functions should go into `libc/common`, but a **significant** effort was made to ensure that external C libraries **do not** have access to `libc/common` as a part of #67048.

"Not naming names" (to quote from last week's TSC meeting), but many reviewers / release managers / maintainers seemed very quick to submit and / or approve of that change. I felt  quite a lot of undue pressure to follow suit and merge it 🤷. I would happily revert it though.

```cmake
if(NOT CONFIG_EXTERNAL_LIBC)
add_subdirectory(libc)
endif()
```

> as a POSIX C library will already provide implementations -- these functions aren't OS specific.

Yes.

Picolibc does provide implementations of all of these. If `CONFIG_PICOLIBC=y`, and if the any of these symbols are not already pulled in by the time the libc is linked, Picolibc's version will be used. I believe the same already goes for Newlib.

Some issues preventing us from using other versions as of today:
* Picolibc currently doese not define `_POSIX_VERSION` when built against Zephyr, even if `_POSIX_C_SOURCE` is defined
* there is currently a bug in newlib's version of `setenv()`, so using the `lib/posix` version is probably a safer bet
* there was a bug in Picolibc's verison of `setenv()` and it will fail tests until `west.yml` and the SDK are updated. For the time being, the `lib/posix` version is probably a safer bet.
* https://github.com/picolibc/picolibc/issues/648

For those reasons, and because I agree that POSIX C libraries can provide those symbols, I only used `imply POSIX_ENV` for shell env service (rather than `select`). Otherwise, `CONFIG_POSIX_ENV` could be set to `n` and the shell env service should work fine (assuming `_POSIX_VERSION` is defined by the implementation).

Aside from `getenv()`, the remainder of these functions have nothing to do with ISO C and probably *should* go into `lib/posix`. The main reasons why I thought it useful to include `getenv()` in the POSIX implementation were

* there was no previous implementation of `getenv()` in the Minimal C library
* there is no requirement for the Minimal C library to have `getenv()`
* it is important that `getenv()`, `setenv()`, `unsetenv()` and `environ` accesses all be synchronized to avoid race conditions (so they should be co-located)
* `getenv()`, `setenv()`, `unsetenv()`, and `environ` are all requirements for PSE51, PSE52, and PSE53 (#51211)
* the commit(s) that fixed Picolibc and updated `west.yml` were in the future (at the time this change was made)

I would be happy to revisit at some point when the other issues are resolved.

issue_context.title: posix: implement `setenv()`
issue_context.body:
This is part of the See [POSIX Roadmap for LTSv3](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/51211) (RFC #51211).

`setenv()` is required as part of `POSIX_SINGLE_PROCESS` [Subprofiling Option Group](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/xrat/V4_subprofiles.html).

For more information, please refer to https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/functions/setenv.html
